s: In which year was Kandla, Asia's first Export Processing Zone, set up?
x: Kandla EPZ was set up in 1965 as India's (and Asia's) first; the SEZ policy came in 2000.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Falta is an Export Processing Zone in West Bengal. SEEPZ is located in Santacruz, Mumbai, while MEPZ is associated with Chennai.

s: With the SEZ framework in force from 2006, which existing units were allowed to convert into Special Economic Zones?
o: Export Processing Zones and Export Oriented Units
National Investment and Manufacturing Zones and Coastal Economic Zones
Industrial corridors and industrial smart cities
x: Existing EPZs and EOUs could convert into SEZs (Kandla, for example, became an SEZ). NIMZs and CEZs are later, separate concepts; corridors and smart cities are not SEZ conversions; FTWZs are a type of SEZ purpose, not a unit that converts.

s: Which of the following is the correct description of a free trade zone?
o: An area reserved exclusively for agricultural exports
An area where goods may be landed, stored, processed and re-exported without customs duty
An area where imported goods must be consumed before re-export
An area where only domestically produced goods may be sold without State taxes
x: A free trade zone permits goods to be landed, stored, processed and re-exported without payment of customs duty.

s: Where is SEEPZ located?
x: SEEPZ is at Santacruz, Mumbai; MEPZ is in Chennai.

s: When was the Surat EPZ converted into an SEZ?
x: Surat, the first private-sector EPZ (1997), became an SEZ on 1 November 2000.

s: In which State is the Falta Export Processing Zone?
x: Falta EPZ is in West Bengal; Kandla is in Gujarat.

s: The Special Economic Zone (SEZ) Policy was announced in April 2000 through which policy framework?
x: The SEZ Policy was announced in April 2000 through the EXIM Policy 2000-01.

s: When did the Special Economic Zones Act receive Presidential assent?
x: The SEZ Act was passed in May 2005, got assent on 23 June 2005 and came into force on 10 February 2006.

s: In 2025, to what was the minimum land for semiconductor and electronic-component SEZs cut?
x: The SEZ (Amendment) Rules 2025 cut the land requirement from 50 ha to 10 ha.

s:
Consider the following statements about the SEZ framework:
1. The SEZ policy was announced in the EXIM Policy 2000-01.
2. The SEZ Act and Rules came into force on 23 June 2005.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The SEZ policy came in EXIM Policy 2000-01; 23 June 2005 is the date of President's assent, and the Act came into force on 10 February 2006.

s: Who among the following may set up an SEZ?
o: The Central or a State Government only
The Central Government, a State Government or any person
x: SEZs may be set up jointly or severally by the Centre, a State or any person, including public, private and joint-sector entities.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Section 18 of SEZ Act – More than one IFSC per SEZ
Section 18 of SEZ Act – Income-tax holiday for SEZ units
Section 18 of SEZ Act – Only one IFSC per SEZ
x: Section 18 of the SEZ Act allows an IFSC in an SEZ, but only one IFSC per SEZ; Section 10AA is the income-tax exemption.

s: Which of the following is a main institutional feature of the SEZ framework?
o: Mandatory clearance only through the Reserve Bank of India
Single-window clearance for Central and State matters
Separate customs clearance for every unit
x: The SEZ framework provides single-window clearance for matters involving both the Central and State Governments.

s: Proposals for setting up SEZs are routed through the State Government to which body for approval?
x: Proposals for SEZs are routed through the State Government to the Board of Approval.

s: During which period were the SEZ income-tax holidays phased out under the sunset clause?
x: The SEZ tax holidays under Section 10AA were phased out during 2017-2020, not 2010-2013.

s: What was the minimum area for a multi-product SEZ under the SEZ Rules 2006?
x: Multi-product SEZs needed 1,000 ha and sector-specific SEZs 100 ha.

s: Up to what limit is FDI allowed in SEZs for most manufacturing activities?
x: 100 per cent FDI is allowed under the automatic route for most manufacturing in SEZs.

s: What is the primary aim of setting up Special Economic Zones in India?
o: Raise tax revenue for State Governments
x: An SEZ is an export-oriented enclave; its primary aim is exports. Employment is a benefit but 'primarily to generate employment' was the wrong option in the APPSC-G2 2017 key. Raising State revenue or giving land to farmers is not its purpose.

s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the SEZ Act, 2005?
o: Promotion of investment from domestic and foreign sources
Promotion of exports of services only
x: The Act aims to promote exports of goods and services, not services only.

s: How much income-tax exemption did SEZ units get for the first five years under Section 10AA of the Income Tax Act?
x: Section 10AA gave 100% exemption for 5 years, 50% for the next 5 and 50% of reinvested profit for 5 more.

s: To what was the minimum area for a sector-specific SEZ reduced in 2019?
x: The Rules of 2006 set 100 ha for sector-specific SEZs; it was cut to 50 ha in 2019.

s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or debate concerning SEZs and industrial policy?
o: Land acquisition, including the Nandigram controversy
Guaranteed expansion of employment in every notified SEZ
x: Land acquisition, revenue loss, under-used land and WTO-inconsistent export subsidies are identified criticisms. Guaranteed employment expansion in every SEZ is not listed as a criticism.

s: Which one of the following was identified as a criticism of the performance of SEZs?
o: SEZs received more than half of total foreign direct investment.
Domestic tariff area sales were completely unrestricted.
SEZs received less than 3% of foreign direct investment.
No SEZ units were shut during the five-year period.
x: SEZs received less than 3% of FDI. Other criticisms included capped DTA sales and the closure of many units.

s: Which State has the largest number of operational SEZs at present?
x: Tamil Nadu has the most operational SEZs now; Telangana has the most approved SEZs.

s: SEZ exports in FY 2024-25 were about what share of India's exports?
x: SEZ exports of about ₹14.64 lakh crore in FY 2024-25 were about 21 per cent of India's exports.

s: Which State has the largest number of approved SEZs at present?
x: Telangana has the most approved SEZs, while Tamil Nadu has the most operational SEZs.

s: In which of the following years did SEZ exports record the highest growth over the previous year?
x: Among these years, SEZ exports grew fastest in 2007-08.

s: Which change is associated with the proposed DESH Bill?
o: Removal of the positive Net Foreign Exchange condition
Mandatory positive NFE for all units
Immediate repeal of the SEZ Act by an enacted law
A ban on Domestic Tariff Area sales
x: The DESH proposal removes the positive NFE condition and allows DTA sales; it is still pending and has not replaced the SEZ Act.

s: What did the Baba Kalyani Committee (2018) recommend renaming SEZs as?
x: The committee recommended renaming SEZs as 3Es—Employment and Economic Enclaves.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about BHAVYA?
o: It has an allocation of ₹33,660 crore.
It is implemented by NICDC through an SPV of NICDIT and a State agency.
It aims to establish 50 plug-and-play industrial parks.
x: BHAVYA aims at 100 plug-and-play industrial parks, not 50; the other statements are correct.

s: The criticism that SEZ incentives may be WTO-inconsistent relates mainly to which of the following?
x: One criticism is that export subsidies associated with SEZs may be inconsistent with WTO obligations.

s: The Nandigram protests of 2007 were against land acquisition for which type of SEZ?
o: Free Trade Warehousing Zone at Kandla
x: Nandigram in West Bengal witnessed violent protests in 2007 against land acquisition for a chemical-hub SEZ.

s: In which Budget was the DESH Bill to replace the SEZ Act announced?
x: The DESH Bill was announced in Budget 2022-23 and is still pending.

s: In which district of West Bengal is Nandigram, the site of the 2007 anti-SEZ protests?
x: Nandigram is in Purba Medinipur district; protests in 2007 opposed land acquisition for a chemical hub.

s: What is the full form of BHAVYA, the 2026 scheme for plug-and-play industrial parks?
x: BHAVYA is Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana, with ₹33,660 crore for 100 parks.

s: What is the full form of DESH in the DESH Bill proposed to replace the SEZ Act?
o: Development of Export and Special Hubs
Development of Enterprise and Services Hubs
Development of Economic and Social Hubs
x: DESH = Development of Enterprise and Services Hubs; announced in Budget 2022-23, still pending.

s: What type of zone is Sri City in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Sri City is a multi-product SEZ in Satyavedu and Varadaiahpalem mandals.

s: What was Visakhapatnam before it became an SEZ?
x: Visakhapatnam was an old EPZ that later became an SEZ.

s: Sri City, a multi-product SEZ of Andhra Pradesh, lies in Varadaiahpalem and which other mandal?
x: Sri City lies in Satyavedu and Varadaiahpalem mandals.

s: Which department and ministry are associated with NICDC?
o: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
Department of Heavy Industry, Ministry of Steel
x: NICDC is associated with DPIIT under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

s: In which State is the operational greenfield industrial smart city of Shendra-Bidkin?
x: Shendra-Bidkin is in Maharashtra; Dholera, the other operational city, is in Gujarat.

s: The Orvakal industrial node in Andhra Pradesh is part of which corridor?
x: Orvakal is on HBIC; Kopparthy is on VCIC and Krishnapatnam on CBIC.

s: Which country is the partner for the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor?
x: DMIC is backed by Japan through JICA and JBIC.

s: Which agency funds the Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor?
x: VCIC is funded by the ADB; DMIC's partner is Japan.

s: Which is India's first coastal industrial corridor?
x: The 800-km Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor is India's first coastal corridor.

s: Which of the following States is NOT covered by the Amritsar-Kolkata Industrial Corridor?
x: AKIC covers Punjab, Haryana, Uttarakhand, UP, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal; Madhya Pradesh is on DMIC.

s: What was NICDC formerly known as?
x: NICDC, under DPIIT, was formerly the DMIC Development Corporation; NICDIT is the trust it advises.

s: The National Industrial Corridor Programme envisages how many industrial corridors?
x: The programme has 11 industrial corridors in 4 phases.

s: Which pair of greenfield industrial smart city and corridor is correctly matched?
x: Kopparthy (Kadapa) is on VCIC, Orvakal (Kurnool) on HBIC and Krishnapatnam (Nellore) on CBIC.

s: Which of the following States is NOT covered by the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor?
x: CBIC (with its Kochi extension) covers Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala, not Maharashtra.

s: Which country prepared the perspective plan of the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor?
x: Japan, through JICA, prepared the CBIC perspective plan; Japan is also the DMIC partner.

s: Of which corridor is the Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor the first phase?
x: VCIC is Phase 1 of the ~2,500 km East Coast Economic Corridor, with ADB as lead partner.

s: Under which industrial corridor is the Krishnapatnam industrial smart city in Nellore being developed?
x: Krishnapatnam (KRIS City) is an AP node of CBIC; Orvakal is HBIC and Kopparthy is VCIC.

s: Which of the following States is NOT covered by the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor?
x: DMIC covers UP, Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP and Maharashtra, not Punjab.

s: In which State is Dholera, an operational greenfield industrial smart city?
x: Dholera is in Gujarat; Shendra-Bidkin is in Maharashtra.

s: What is the approximate length of the Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor, Phase 1 of the East Coast Economic Corridor?
x: VCIC is about 800 km; the whole East Coast Economic Corridor is about 2,500 km.

s: Which of the following is a node of the Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor?
x: VCIC nodes include Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Amaravati and Yerpedu-Srikalahasti; Orvakal is on HBIC.

s: Coastal Economic Zones were proposed under which programme's port-led industrialisation pillar?
x: The 14 CEZs, port-proximate clusters and SEZs, were proposed under Sagarmala's port-led industrialisation pillar.

s: How many Coastal Economic Zones were proposed under the Sagarmala National Perspective Plan?
x: The Sagarmala National Perspective Plan (2016) proposed 14 CEZs.

s: In which year was the Sagarmala National Perspective Plan, which proposed Coastal Economic Zones, released?
x: The Sagarmala National Perspective Plan of 2016 proposed 14 CEZs under port-led industrialisation.

s: What is the full form of ULIP in the context of logistics infrastructure?
x: ULIP stands for Unified Logistics Interface Platform.

s: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of Sagarmala?
x: Sagarmala's pillars include port modernisation, port connectivity, port-led industrialisation, coastal community development, and coastal shipping and inland water transport.

s: In which year was Sagarmala 2.0 introduced?
x: Sagarmala (800-plus projects, about ₹5.8 lakh crore) was followed by Sagarmala 2.0 in 2025.

s:
Consider the following statements about Phase I of Bharatmala Pariyojana:
1. It was launched in 2017.
2. Its coverage extends to more than 580 districts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: Phase I came in 2017 and covers 34,800 km across 580+ districts.

s: In which year was the National Perspective Plan of Sagarmala released?
x: Sagarmala's National Perspective Plan came in 2016; Bharatmala was launched in 2017 and Sagarmala 2.0 in 2025.

s: What length is covered by Phase-I of Bharatmala Pariyojana?
x: Bharatmala Phase-I covers about 34,800 km across more than 580 districts.

s: With which sector is the Sagarmala programme related?
x: Sagarmala is about port-led development; Bharatmala is about roads.

s: To what level does the National Rail Plan 2030 seek to raise the railways' share in freight from 28%?
x: The National Rail Plan 2030 aims to raise rail's freight share from 28% to 45% and to expand Kavach.

s: Which agency funds the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor?
x: The Western DFC is associated with JICA, while the 1,337 km Eastern DFC is associated with the World Bank.

s:
Consider the following statements about railway electrification in India:
1. About 50.91% of routes were electrified by March 2019.
2. About 99.1% of broad-gauge routes were electrified by October 2025.
3. 100% of broad-gauge routes were electrified by October 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Electrification rose from 50.91% of routes (March 2019) to 99.1% of broad-gauge routes by October 2025, not 100%.

s: Which agency funds the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor (1,337 km)?
x: The Eastern DFC is World Bank-funded; the Western DFC is associated with JICA.

s: On which World Bank index is the LEADS index, introduced by DPIIT in 2018, modelled?
x: LEADS is modelled on the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index, not the Ease of Doing Business Index.

s: By which year does the National Logistics Policy 2022 aim to bring logistics cost down to single digits of GDP?
x: The National Logistics Policy targets logistics cost in single digits of GDP by 2030.

s: In which category was Andhra Pradesh placed among coastal States in LEADS 2023?
x: AP was an 'Achiever' among coastal States in LEADS 2023.

s: India's logistics cost in FY24 was estimated at about what share of GDP?
x: Logistics cost fell to 7.97% of GDP in FY24 from 8.84% in FY23; older estimates were 13-14%.

s: Which of the following States was placed among the 'Exemplars' in LEADS 2025?
x: LEADS 2025 Exemplars included Tamil Nadu, UP, Mizoram and Delhi.

s: What was the investment envisaged under the National Infrastructure Pipeline (FY2019-20 to FY2024-25)?
x: The NIP envisaged about ₹111 lakh crore across both economic and social infrastructure.

s: What is the estimated multiplier of infrastructure capital expenditure?
x: The infrastructure capital expenditure multiplier is estimated at approximately 2.5–3.5.

s: Which sector has the largest share in the National Infrastructure Pipeline?
x: Energy has about 24% of NIP, ahead of roads (~18%), urban (~17%) and railways (~12%).

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Infrastructure Pipeline:
1. It covers only economic infrastructure.
2. States were to fund about 40% of it.
3. The private sector was to fund about 21% of it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: NIP covers both economic and social infrastructure, so 1 is wrong; the split is Centre 39%, States 40%, private 21%.

s: What was the Centre's share in funding the National Infrastructure Pipeline?
x: NIP funding: Centre 39%, States 40% and private sector 21%.

s: On which Invest India platform are National Infrastructure Pipeline projects shown to investors?
x: NIP projects are showcased to investors on the India Investment Grid (IIG) of Invest India.

s: What is the Centre's capital expenditure in the Union Budget 2026-27?
x: Centre's capex rose from ₹5.92 lakh crore (FY22) to ₹11.21 lakh crore (FY26) and ₹12.2 lakh crore in Budget 2026-27.

s: What is the paid-up capital of NaBFID, set up under the NaBFID Act, 2021?
x: NaBFID was established under the NaBFID Act, 2021 with Rs 20,000 crore paid-up capital and a Rs 5,000 crore grant.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NIIF – Created by an Act of Parliament in 2021
x: IIFCL (2006) has been an NBFC-IFC since 2013; NIIF was set up in 2015 and NaBFID was created by the NaBFID Act, 2021.

s: What did the Vijay Kelkar Committee (2015) deal with?
o: Revisiting and revitalising the PPP model
x: The Kelkar Committee (2015) reviewed the PPP model; the Deepak Parekh Committee dealt with infrastructure financing.

s: Which category of funds does the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF), set up in 2015, manage?
x: NIIF is a government-anchored fund set up in 2015 that manages Category II AIFs.

s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. NaBFID Act
2. IIFCL set up
3. NIIF set up
4. SEBI InvIT regulations
x: IIFCL 2006, InvIT regulations 2014, NIIF 2015 and NaBFID Act 2021.

s: Who headed the committee on financing of infrastructure that reported in May 2007?
x: The Deepak Parekh Committee on financing infrastructure reported in May 2007; Kelkar (2015) reviewed PPPs.

s: Which committee proposed an Infrastructure PPP Adjudication Tribunal?
x: The Kelkar Committee (2015) on revitalising PPPs proposed this tribunal and a PPP Project Review Committee.

s: Which was the first airport in India built under PPP?
x: Cochin International Airport, owned by the company CIAL, was India's first PPP airport and the world's first fully solar-powered airport (2015).

s: Which is India's first dedicated deep-water transhipment port?
x: Vizhinjam in Kerala, developed by Adani Ports under PPP, was commissioned on 2 May 2025.

s: When did Navi Mumbai International Airport begin commercial operations?
x: Navi Mumbai airport (Adani 74%, CIDCO 26%) began commercial operations on 25 December 2025.

s: Which airport became the world's first fully solar-powered airport in 2015?
x: Cochin International Airport, owned by CIAL, became the world's first fully solar-powered airport in 2015.

s: In which State is Vizhinjam, India's first dedicated deep-water transhipment port?
x: Vizhinjam is in Kerala; Adani Ports built it under PPP and it was commissioned on 2 May 2025.

s: What is PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan?
x: PM Gati Shakti is a whole-of-government, GIS-based integrated planning initiative for infrastructure development.

s: Who developed the National Master Plan portal of PM Gati Shakti?
x: The portal, containing more than 1,700 data layers, was developed by BISAG-N of Gandhinagar.

s: Which one of the following is NOT among the seven engines of PM Gati Shakti?
x: The seven engines are Railways, Roads, Ports, Waterways, Airports, Mass Transport and Logistics Infrastructure (APPSC-GS 2024 key). Power transmission is not one of them.

s: How many ministries are brought onto one digital platform under PM Gati Shakti?
x: PM Gati Shakti integrates 16 ministries, including Railways, Roads and Ports; 7 is the number of engines.

s: Who heads the Empowered Group of Secretaries under PM Gati Shakti?
x: The Empowered Group of Secretaries, headed by the Cabinet Secretary, sits above the Network Planning Group.

s: In which year was the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan launched?
x: PM GatiShakti was launched on 13 October 2021.

s: When was the National Logistics Policy, complementing PM GatiShakti, launched?
x: The NLP was launched in September 2022 to bring logistics cost to single digits of GDP by 2030.

s: Which assets does the National Monetisation Pipeline monetise?
o: Greenfield assets, with ownership transferred to buyers
Brownfield assets, with ownership permanently transferred
Brownfield core infrastructure assets, with ownership retained by the Government
Greenfield assets, with ownership retained by the Government
x: The NMP monetises brownfield core infrastructure while ownership remains with the Government.

s: What is the value of National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0 (FY26-FY30)?
x: NMP 2.0 is valued at ₹16.72 lakh crore (including ₹5.8 lakh crore of private participation); NMP 1.0 was ₹6 lakh crore.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0 (FY26-FY30):
1. It was prepared by NITI Aayog.
2. Highways, MMLPs and ropeways have the largest share in it.
3. Railways have a larger share in it than power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: NMP 2.0 was prepared by NITI Aayog and highways/MMLPs/ropeways lead with 26%; power (17%) is ahead of railways (16%), so 3 is wrong.

s: In which Union Budget was the National Monetisation Pipeline announced?
x: The National Monetisation Pipeline was announced in the Union Budget 2021-22.

s: In NMP 1.0, which sector actually yielded the most monetisation proceeds?
x: Roads were the largest planned sector of NMP 1.0, but coal gave the most actual money (about ₹2 lakh crore).

s: What was the total value of the National Monetisation Pipeline 1.0 (FY22-FY25)?
x: NMP 1.0 was ₹6 lakh crore; about ₹5.3 lakh crore was monetised.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's Blue Economy target?
x: Andhra Pradesh has set a Blue Economy target of US$20 billion by 2035.

s: Andhra Pradesh's coastline is about how long, and what is its rank among Indian States?
x: Andhra Pradesh has a coastline of about 1,053.07 km, the 3rd longest in India. The other length/rank combinations are wrong.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Machilipatnam is located in Krishna district. Ramayapatnam is in Nellore, Mulapeta is in Srikakulam and Kakinada SEZ port is in Kakinada district.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with regard to operational PPP ports in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Krishnapatnam is associated with BOST and 2004. Gangavaram is associated with BOOT and 2003, while Kakinada Deep Water is also an operational PPP port.

s: Bhogapuram airport near Visakhapatnam is being developed by GMR under which model?
x: GMR is developing Bhogapuram airport through GVIAL under the PPP-DBFOT model, with a 3,800-metre runway.

s: Why is Orvakal/Kurnool airport notable?
o: The first international airport of Andhra Pradesh, in 2021
The first airport in India built under the PPP-DBFOT model, in 2022
The first airport built by GMR in coastal Andhra Pradesh, in 2020
The first airport in South India built entirely by a State, in 2021
x: Orvakal/Kurnool airport was the first airport in South India built entirely by a State, and it was completed in 2021.

s: By 2030, Andhra Pradesh aims to have which combination of infrastructure?
o: Four greenfield ports and eleven fishing harbours
Eleven greenfield ports and four fishing harbours
Three greenfield ports and seventeen fishing harbours
Four major ports and eleven airports
x: The target for 2030 is four greenfield ports and eleven fishing harbours.

s: The Mulapeta (Bhavanapadu) greenfield port is located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Mulapeta is in Srikakulam; Ramayapatnam is in Nellore and Machilipatnam in Krishna.

s: Which body handles port development, maritime infrastructure and coastal logistics in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The AP Maritime Board (APMB) handles port development, maritime infrastructure and coastal logistics in the State.

s: What is the planned length of the runway of Bhogapuram airport near Visakhapatnam?
x: Bhogapuram airport, developed by GMR under PPP-DBFOT, has a 3,800 m runway.

s: Which company is developing the Machilipatnam greenfield port in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Machilipatnam port (Krishna district) is being developed by MEIL under the landlord model.

s: Which is the largest private port in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Krishnapatnam (BOST, 2004) is the largest private port in AP.

s: Which of the following is NOT an international airport of Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP's three international airports are Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati; Kadapa is domestic.

s: The Electricity Act, 2003 replaced the Indian Electricity Act, 1910, the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948 and which other law?
x: The 2003 Act replaced the 1910 Act, the 1948 Supply Act and the Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act, 1998.

s: Under which Section of the Electricity Act, 2003 are tariffs determined through competitive bidding?
x: Section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003 provides for adoption of tariff determined through a transparent process of bidding in accordance with guidelines issued by the Central Government.

s: India's AT&C losses fell from 22.62% in FY14 to what level in FY25?
x: AT&C losses fell to 15.04% in FY25, and the demand-supply gap fell from 4.2% to zero by November 2025.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
x: RDSS targets reduction of AT&C losses and smart metering; rural feeder separation is DDUGJY.

s: Under UDAY, States were to take over what share of DISCOM debt?
x: UDAY (2015) required States to take over 75% of DISCOM debt.

s: Which of the following was a demand-side measure under UDAY?
o: Smart metering to cut AT&C losses
x: UDAY's demand-side step was promoting LED bulbs; feeder separation is DDUGJY, households is Saubhagya and smart metering is RDSS.

s:
Arrange the following schemes in chronological order of launch:
1. Saubhagya
2. DDUGJY
3. RDSS
4. UDAY
x: DDUGJY 2014, UDAY 2015, Saubhagya 2017, RDSS 2021.

s: Under UDAY (November 2015), States took over what share of DISCOM debt?
x: UDAY shifted 75% of DISCOM debt to the States; RDSS came later, in 2021.

s: Against an estimated battery-storage need of 336 GWh by 2029-30, how much battery storage did India have in September 2025?
x: India had only about 500 MWh of battery storage in September 2025 against a requirement of 336 GWh by 2029-30.

s: As of 31 July 2026, non-fossil sources made up about what share of India's installed power capacity?
x: Of about 552 GW, non-fossil capacity was 300.5 GW, over 54%.

s: Which energy type has the largest installed capacity within India's non-fossil power mix?
x: Solar (164.59 GW) leads, ahead of wind (58.14 GW), hydro (57.24 GW) and nuclear (8.78 GW).

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's installed power capacity on 31 July 2025?
x: AP had 27,586.93 MW, of which thermal was 13,907.67 MW and RE 13,488.39 MW.

s: Which company operates India's nuclear power reactors?
x: Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) runs the reactors.

s: Which is the nodal agency of the Andhra Pradesh Solar Power Policy, 2018?
x: NREDCAP is the nodal agency; the policy notes the State has about 300 sunny days a year.

s: PM-KUSUM in Andhra Pradesh covers about how many pumps?
x: PM-KUSUM in Andhra Pradesh covers 2.93 lakh pumps.

s: In which year was Andhra Pradesh's Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy issued?
x: The Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy, 2023 aims to make Andhra Pradesh a global green hydrogen hub.

s: The AP Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy 2023 targets how much green hydrogen in five years?
x: It targets 0.5 MTPA green hydrogen and 2 MTPA green ammonia in five years.

s: How much pumped storage potential does the AP Pumped Storage Power Promotion Policy 2022 seek to harness?
x: The policy aims to harness about 33 GW of pumped storage potential in AP.

s: Which Andhra Pradesh policy brings renewable energy, pumped storage, green hydrogen, biofuels and EV charging under one framework?
o: AP Pumped Storage Power Promotion Policy 2022
AP Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy 2023
x: The AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy 2024 gives one framework for all clean-energy segments.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: PNGRB — downstream oil and gas regulation
x: APGENCO is responsible for State electricity generation, not distribution. Distribution is performed by the DISCOMs, while APTRANSCO handles transmission.

s: Which body is responsible for technical planning and generation adequacy plans in India's power sector?
o: Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB)
x: The CEA handles technical planning and generation adequacy plans. CERC sets central and inter-State tariffs (APERC for the State), PNGRB regulates downstream oil and gas, and BEE runs star labelling.

s: APERC approved how much coal power through Section 63 DBFOO bidding as the first phase of Andhra Pradesh's plan?
x: APERC approved 1,600 MW, the first phase of a planned 5,588 MW by 2035-36.

s: Which body does star labelling of electrical appliances in India?
x: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) runs star labelling; CEA does technical planning.

s: Which body fixes Central and inter-State electricity tariffs?
x: CERC fixes central and inter-State tariffs; APERC fixes State tariffs in AP.

s: Under which ministry does IREDA, which finances renewable energy and energy-efficiency projects, work?
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
x: IREDA is under MNRE and has been a Navratna since 2024.

s: In which year was the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board Act passed?
x: PNGRB was set up under the PNGRB Act, 2006, to regulate downstream oil and gas.

s: Since 2024, which status does IREDA hold?
x: IREDA, under MNRE, became a Navratna in 2024; earlier it was a Mini Ratna.

s: What was the original 2010 solar capacity target of the Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission?
x: JNNSM began with a 20 GW target, raised in 2015 to 100 GW (40 GW rooftop + 60 GW large/medium).

s: By which year was India's 175 GW renewable-energy target to be achieved?
x: The 175 GW target was for 2022; the First NDC targets applied to 2030.

s: The National Green Hydrogen Mission has set a target of producing how much green hydrogen annually by 2030?
x: The National Green Hydrogen Mission targets production of 5 million metric tonnes of green hydrogen per year by 2030.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's COP26 (2021) commitments?
o: India declared a net-zero target for 2070.
India announced 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030.
Both pledges form part of the Panchamrit commitments.
The 500 GW target is the reason for the 2070 net-zero goal.
x: The 2030 capacity target is a separate Panchamrit pledge, not the reason for the 2070 net-zero goal.

s: Of the revised 100 GW solar target, how much was earmarked for rooftop solar?
x: The 100 GW target was split into 40 GW rooftop and 60 GW large and medium projects.

s: The Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission is one of how many missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change?
x: JNNSM (2010) is one of the 8 missions of the NAPCC.

s: Under India's first NDC, what share of installed power capacity was to come from non-fossil sources by 2030?
x: The first NDC promised over 40% non-fossil capacity by 2030; COP26 raised it to 50% of requirement from RE.

s: In which year was the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, under which non-coking coal mines were nationalised, passed?
x: Coking coal mines were nationalised in 1971-72 and non-coking mines under the 1973 Act.

s: How are coal blocks allocated under the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015?
x: After the Supreme Court cancelled coal block allocations, the 2015 Act provided allocation by auction, run by the Nominated Authority.

s: What does the Coal Controller's Organisation, headquartered at Kolkata, mainly check?
x: The Coal Controller's Organisation checks coal quality and grading, settles quality complaints and collects coal statistics.

s: Who publishes the annual 'Energy Statistics India'?
x: Energy Statistics India is published by the NSO under MoSPI, not NITI Aayog.

s: Which body conducts coal block auctions under the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015?
x: Auctions under the 2015 Act are run by the Nominated Authority of the Ministry of Coal.

s: Which of the following is the main reason why India imports coking coal despite large coal reserves?
o: Domestic coal is costlier to mine than imported coal
Supply of high-quality low-ash coking coal in India is limited
Exports of domestic coal are compulsory
Coal mining is banned in most States
x: Domestic supply of low-ash coking coal is limited, and plants designed on imported coal cannot use domestic coal.

s: Under which import regime is coal kept in India's import policy?
x: Coal is under Open General Licence; consumers may import from any source on paying duty.

s: Who chairs the National Biofuel Coordination Committee?
o: Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Minister of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare
Minister of New and Renewable Energy
x: The Petroleum Minister chairs the National Biofuel Coordination Committee, which approves the use of surplus food grains for ethanol.

s: Under the National Policy on Biofuels, 2018 (as amended in 2022) and the Ethanol Blended Petrol programme, India set which ethanol-blending target?
x: The target is 20% ethanol blending by 2025, meant to cut oil imports and help sugarcane farmers. The other percentage/year pairs are not the stated target.

s: Which of the following is a permitted feedstock for ethanol production in India?
x: Ethanol feedstocks include sugarcane juice, sugar beet, sweet sorghum, damaged food grains, maize and cassava.

s: In which year did India achieve 20% ethanol blending in petrol (E20)?
x: The 20% blending target set for 2025 was achieved in 2025.

s: A proposal is made to use surplus food grains for ethanol production. Which body is responsible for approving such use?
x: Approval for using surplus food grains for ethanol is given by the National Biofuel Coordination Committee.

s: The MNRE's Solar Park Scheme mainly makes which of the following available to developers?
o: Feed-in tariff guarantees and tax holidays
x: The Solar Park Scheme facilitates solar development by providing land and transmission infrastructure to developers.

s: India's largest thermal power plant, Vindhyachal (NTPC), is located in which State and has what capacity?
x: Vindhyachal (NTPC), the largest thermal plant, is in Madhya Pradesh with 4,760 MW. 1,000 MW is the Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park in Andhra Pradesh; Vindhyachal is not in Uttar Pradesh.

s: What is the capacity of the Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park is 1,000 MW.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Kudankulam is in Tamil Nadu; Tehri is in Uttarakhand, Koyna in Maharashtra and Vindhyachal in Madhya Pradesh.

s: Which is the largest hydro power complex in India by capacity?
x: The Tehri complex in Uttarakhand (2,400 MW) is the largest hydro by capacity.

s: In which State is the Koyna hydroelectric project, the largest completed hydro project in India?
x: Koyna (1,960 MW) is in Maharashtra.

s: From which coalfields does NTPC Korba get its coal?
x: NTPC Korba in Chhattisgarh gets coal from the Kusmunda and Gevra mines.

s: India meets roughly what share of its petroleum requirement through imports?
x: India imports more than 80% of its petroleum requirement.

s: Which of the following is the correct set of locations of India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPRs)?
x: The Strategic Petroleum Reserves mentioned are located at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur.

s: India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves provide about how many days of import cover?
x: India's SPRs give about 9.5 days of import cover, far below the IEA norm of 90 days.

s: When were diesel prices in India decontrolled?
x: Petrol was decontrolled on 26 June 2010 and diesel on 19 October 2014.

s: India imports roughly what share of its gas requirement?
x: India imports about 50% of its gas, against about 85% of its petroleum.

s: Which type of contract did the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP), 2016 bring in place of production-sharing contracts?
x: HELP replaced NELP and uses revenue-sharing contracts with a single licence for all hydrocarbons.

s: From which country does India import hydropower from projects such as Chukha, Tala and Mangdechhu?
x: India imports hydropower from Bhutan's Chukha, Tala, Kurichhu and Mangdechhu projects.

s: When were petrol prices in India decontrolled?
x: Petrol was decontrolled on 26 June 2010; diesel on 19 October 2014.

s: How many days of net imports does the International Energy Agency norm require countries to hold as oil stocks?
x: The IEA norm is 90 days; India's SPRs give about 9.5 days.

s: Who coined the expression 'Licence-Permit-Quota Raj' for the pre-1991 regime of controls in India?
x: C. Rajagopalachari coined 'Licence-Permit-Quota Raj' to criticise the control regime that was a long-term cause of the 1991 crisis. Nehru led the planned economy, Mahalanobis designed the Second Plan model, and Raja Chelliah headed the 1991 tax reform committee.

s: Who is widely called the 'father of Indian economic reforms'?
x: P.V. Narasimha Rao is called the father of Indian economic reforms; Dr. Manmohan Singh is regarded as the architect of liberalisation.

s: With which of the following was the Narasimham Committee of 1991 mainly concerned?
o: Industrial licensing and foreign trade quotas
Financial-sector reform, including interest deregulation and private banks
x: The Narasimham Committee focused on financial-sector reform, including interest deregulation and the development of private banks such as HDFC and ICICI.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: C. Rangarajan Committee – Disinvestment of PSUs
R.N. Malhotra Committee – Capital account convertibility
x: Rangarajan dealt with PSU disinvestment, Chelliah with tax reforms, Malhotra with insurance and Tarapore with capital account convertibility.

s: Who headed the 1997 committee on capital account convertibility?
x: The Tarapore Committee (report 30 May 1997) gave a 3-phase roadmap for capital account convertibility.

s: When did P.V. Narasimha Rao take office as Prime Minister?
x: Rao became PM on 21 June 1991; devaluation came on 1 and 3 July and the Industrial Policy on 24 July 1991.

s: Who was the Finance Minister of India when the 1991 economic reforms were introduced?
x: Dr. Manmohan Singh, Finance Minister under P.V. Narasimha Rao, was the architect of the 1991 reforms.

s: Who headed the 1991 committee on tax reforms?
x: The Raja J. Chelliah Committee (1991) recommended lower tax rates and a wider tax base.

s: What is the reduction of tariffs and quantitative restrictions under the 1991 reforms called?
x: Import liberalisation cut tariffs and QRs; de-licensing ended licensing, disinvestment sold PSE equity, globalisation integrated India with the world.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Liberalisation reduces domestic controls through industrial de-licensing, import deregulation and private-sector expansion.

s: Which of the following best describes free trade?
o: Reduction or removal of trade barriers
Provision of an internationally competitive environment
Creation of a level playing field for exports
x: Free trade means reducing or removing trade barriers such as tariffs and quotas. The other options are SEZ objectives.

s: What is the integration of the domestic economy with the world economy, with greater participation of MNCs, called?
x: Globalisation linked India to the world economy through trade, FDI and technology flows and drew in more MNCs.

s: How did the growth of India's IT and outsourcing exports after 1991 help the economy?
x: IT and outsourcing generated services exports that helped cushion India's current account deficit.

s: Which of the following reflects the post-1991 reform direction?
o: Raising tariffs to protect domestic producers
Expanding the list of industries reserved for the public sector
Inviting FDI and FPI, with IT and services exports acting as a cushion
Restricting foreign investment to joint ventures with PSUs
x: The post-reform approach lowered tariffs, invited FDI and FPI, and benefited from IT and services exports as a cushion.

s: How did India's imports behave after globalisation?
x: Globalisation expanded trade and technology access, but imports grew faster than exports.

s: Which of the following is a measure of privatisation rather than globalisation?
x: Disinvestment of PSU equity is privatisation; lower import duties, no import licensing and free FDI are globalisation.

s: After the financial-sector reforms, the RBI was expected to shift from being a regulator to being what?
x: The reforms envisaged the RBI moving from direct regulation towards facilitation of the financial system.

s: How many public sector undertakings were given Navratna status when the scheme was introduced?
x: The Navratna scheme initially covered nine PSUs, distinct from the 97 Miniratnas.

s: Which statement correctly relates liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation?
o: Globalisation is an outcome of liberalisation and privatisation, with outsourcing as a major feature.
Privatisation is the outcome of globalisation, and liberalisation means only export promotion.
Liberalisation and privatisation prohibit international technology flows.
Globalisation is independent of both, and outsourcing is unrelated to it.
x: Globalisation is described as the outcome of liberalisation and privatisation, and outsourcing is its major feature.

s: What is the sharp reduction in the list of industries reserved for the public sector in 1991 known as?
x: Dereservation means reducing the industries reserved for the public sector and opening them to private participation.

s: LPG reforms were associated with which of the following?
x: The LPG reforms opened the door to multinational corporations. Licensing, the joint sector and public-sector dominance belong to the pre-1991 policies.

s: What happened to tax rates and the tax base under the post-1991 liberalisation measures?
x: Tax rates were cut and the base widened, alongside scrapping MRTP asset limits, deregulating interest rates and allowing private banks.

s: Why was disinvestment of PSU equity first undertaken under the 1991 reforms?
x: Disinvestment was first used to bridge the fiscal deficit and only later for efficiency; nationalisation was not part of the NEP.

s: Under privatisation after 1991, above what share of PSU equity did private buyers take over ownership and management?
x: Private buyers acquiring above 51% of a PSU took over its ownership and management.

s: Which is described as a major feature of globalisation?
x: Globalisation is the outcome of liberalisation and privatisation, and outsourcing is its major feature.

s: Which of the following was NOT a part of the New Economic Policy of 1991?
x: Nationalisation is the opposite of the 1991 reforms; delicensing, disinvestment and automatic-route FDI were part of it.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 1991 reforms:
1. FDI in retail and defence was opened in 1991 itself.
2. Full capital account convertibility was not adopted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: FDI in retail and defence came much later, and the capital account is still only partly convertible.

s: In which year was Navratna status first given to public sector enterprises?
x: Navratna status was given to 9 PSUs in 1997.

s: About how many tonnes of gold in all did India pledge during the 1991 BoP crisis?
x: About 67 tonnes were pledged to the Bank of England and UBS, along with an IMF loan and devaluation.

s: What was the main immediate purpose of the 1991 rupee devaluation?
o: Increase the price of Indian exports in foreign markets
Make Indian exports cheaper and help correct the balance of payments
Finance the fiscal deficit through currency expansion
x: Devaluation makes domestic goods relatively cheaper for foreign buyers and was undertaken to help address the balance of payments crisis.

s:
Arrange the following measures in the order in which they occurred during the initial 1991 reform sequence:
A. Industrial delicensing
B. Devaluation of the rupee
C. Removal of import quotas and EXIM scrips
D. Market-determined exchange rate
x: Devaluation came first in July 1991, followed by industrial delicensing, removal of EXIM scrips and import quotas, and the market-determined exchange rate in 1993.

s: In which years did India's demonetisations take place?
x: Demonetisation was not a 1991 measure; India demonetised in 1978 and 2016.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 1991 New Economic Policy?
o: Full capital-account convertibility was not adopted.
Devaluation, tariff cuts and removal of import quotas were external-sector measures.
FDI was liberalised through an automatic route in high-priority industries.
Demonetisation formed part of the 1991 reform package.
x: Demonetisation was not part of the 1991 package; India's demonetisations were in 1978 and 2016.

s: With which central bank did the RBI pledge about 47 tonnes of gold during the 1991 crisis?
o: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
x: About 47 tonnes were pledged by the RBI with the Bank of England (and Bank of Japan); 20 tonnes went via SBI to UBS.

s: In May 1991, through which bank were about 20 tonnes of gold sold with a repurchase option to UBS?
x: About 20 tonnes went via SBI to UBS; the RBI pledged about 47 tonnes with the Bank of England and Bank of Japan.

s: India accepted the obligations of which Article of the IMF Agreement when it made the rupee convertible on current account in August 1994?
x: Current account convertibility came in August 1994 under IMF Article VIII.

s: How large was the IMF Stand-By Arrangement approved for India in October 1991?
x: The IMF Board approved a 20-month Stand-By Arrangement of SDR 1,656 million on 31 October 1991.

s: For how long was the IMF Stand-By Arrangement of October 1991 given to India?
x: The Stand-By Arrangement of SDR 1,656 million ran for 20 months, covering 1991-92 and 1992-93.

s: What were India's foreign exchange reserves in June 1991?
o: $975 million, sufficient for about two weeks of imports
$69.3 billion, sufficient for about one year of imports
$22.8 billion, sufficient for about three months of imports
$9.75 billion, sufficient for about six months of imports
x: India's foreign exchange reserves stood at approximately $975 million in June 1991, covering only about two weeks of imports.

s:
Assertion (A): Civil aviation saw the entry of private airlines after the 1991 reforms.
Reason (R): Power distribution underwent complete and uncontested privatisation.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Private airlines did enter civil aviation, but power-distribution privatisation remained debated, so R is false.

s: What was India's GDP growth in 1994-95?
x: Growth was below 1% in 1991–92, about 5% in 1992–94 and 6.3% in 1994–95.

s: Foreign-exchange reserves rose from about $975 million in 1991 to what level?
x: Foreign-exchange reserves rose from about $975 million in 1991 to approximately $701.4 billion, providing around 11 months of import cover as stated.

s: Which sector remained largely a state monopoly after the 1991 reforms?
x: Railways stayed largely a state monopoly, while telecom, banking and civil aviation were opened up.

s: Which of the following sectors saw private and foreign entry after the 1991 reforms?
x: Telecommunications was reshaped by private and foreign entry; railways, power distribution and ports changed little.

s: What happened to the share of agriculture in India's GDP after the 1991 reforms?
o: It first fell and then rose back to its 1991 level
x: Agriculture's share fell from about 30% in 1991 to about one-fifth now.

s: Which sector became the largest sector of the Indian economy after the 1991 reforms?
x: After 1991 the share of agriculture fell and services became the largest sector.

s: Which statement correctly relates Rajiv Gandhi's reforms to those of 1991?
o: Liberalisation began in the 1980s, but the 1991 reforms were far more comprehensive.
Rajiv Gandhi introduced the complete 1991 package.
The 1991 reforms merely continued an unchanged policy of the 1960s.
x: Some liberalisation began under Rajiv Gandhi in the 1980s, but the 1991 programme was much more comprehensive.

s: Which one of the following represents a long-term cause rather than an immediate trigger of the 1991 crisis?
o: Persistent fiscal profligacy and rising fiscal deficit
x: Persistent fiscal profligacy was a long-term domestic structural cause. The other three were immediate external-financing or geopolitical pressures.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the causes of India's 1991 balance of payments crisis?
o: The Gulf War led to a doubling of oil prices.
Current account deficits had been financed by foreign borrowing since the 1980s.
Remittances from the Gulf region rose sharply.
x: Gulf remittances dried up rather than rising; the other three were causes of the crisis.

s: Which of the following was a feature of the economic groundwork laid during the 1980s?
o: Complete abolition of all industrial licensing
Broad-banding of licences and easier imports of capital goods
x: The 1980s saw broad-banding of licences, easier capital-goods imports, a higher MRTP limit and relaxation of FERA. Complete delicensing and FEMA came later.

s: India's share in world exports fell from 2.2% in 1948 to what level in 1983?
x: Weak exports cut India's world export share from 2.2% (1948) to 0.5% (1983).

s: What happened to remittances from the Gulf to India after the Gulf War of August 1990?
x: The Gulf War doubled oil prices and dried up Gulf remittances; they did not rise.

s: Whose government fell in 1991, just before the New Economic Policy?
x: Political instability (two changes of government, Dec 1989 - June 1991) ended with the fall of Chandra Shekhar's government.

s: In the 1980s, India's growth broke the 'Hindu rate of growth' and reached about what level?
x: Growth touched about 5.5% in the 1980s, but it was debt-fuelled.

s: What was the gross fiscal deficit of the Centre in 1990-91?
x: The Centre's gross fiscal deficit was 8.4 per cent of GDP in 1990-91, compared with 6.1 per cent in 1980-81. The 9.4 per cent figure refers to the combined Centre and States figure.

s: What was the combined fiscal deficit of the Centre and States in 1990-91?
x: 9.4% was the Centre + States fiscal deficit; 8.4% was the Centre's gross fiscal deficit.

s: What was India's GDP growth rate in 1990-91?
x: GDP growth fell to 1.1% in 1990-91 and below 1% in 1991-92.

s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of India's 1991 economic crisis?
x: The crisis had high inflation, low reserves and a large fiscal deficit; the current account was in deficit (about 3.1% of GDP).

s: What was India's current account deficit as a share of GDP in 1990-91?
x: The CAD was 3.1-3.2% of GDP in 1990-91.

s: In which year did the Indian rupee become convertible on the current account?
x: The rupee became market-determined in 1993 and current-account convertible in 1994; capital-account convertibility stayed partial.

s: When did India remove its remaining quantitative restrictions on imports?
x: The remaining QRs went in April 2001; average tariffs fell from about 125% to about 30% and general customs duty was later cut to 10%.

s: When was the Liberalised Exchange Rate Management System (LERMS) introduced?
x: LERMS came in March 1992 (60% at market rate, 40% at official rate); a unified market rate followed in March 1993.

s: In which year was SEBI given statutory status?
x: SEBI received statutory status in 1992; FEMA replaced FERA in 1999.

s: In which year did India become a founding member of the WTO?
x: India was a founding member of the WTO in 1995; the WTO succeeded GATT (1948).

s: Under LERMS (March 1992), what share of export earnings could be converted at the market rate?
x: LERMS was a dual rate: 60% of export earnings at the market rate and 40% at the official rate.

s: India's average import tariff fell from about 125% in the late 1980s to what level by the early 2000s?
x: Average import tariffs fell from about 125% to about 30%; the general customs duty later fell to 10%.

s: In which year was FERA replaced by FEMA?
x: FERA gave way to FEMA in 1999, after convertibility (1994) and WTO membership (1995).

s: As part of which of the following was the strategy of export-led growth introduced in India?
o: The Second Five Year Plan's Mahalanobis model
The Green Revolution strategy of the 1960s
x: Export-led growth came with the 1991 LPG reforms, which moved India from import substitution to export promotion. The Mahalanobis model of the Second Plan was based on heavy industry and import substitution. The Green Revolution was about farm output, and bank nationalisation in 1969 was about state control of credit.

s: In which year did India adopt a unified market-determined exchange rate?
x: LERMS (March 1992) gave a dual rate; a unified market-determined rate came in March 1993.

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Current account convertibility
2. LERMS
3. FERA replaced by FEMA
4. Unified market-determined exchange rate
x: LERMS 1992, market rate 1993, current account convertibility 1994, FEMA 1999.

s: Which organisation did the WTO replace in 1995?
x: The WTO (1995) replaced GATT, set up in 1948 with 23 countries.

s: The Mahalanobis model of the Second Five Year Plan stressed which of the following?
x: The Mahalanobis model stressed heavy industry and import substitution; export promotion came with the 1991 reforms.

s: Which of the following was NOT an element of the Washington Consensus?
x: Privatisation, deregulation and property rights were among the ten Washington Consensus rules; expanding import quotas was not.

s: What is the basic nature of stabilisation measures under the New Economic Policy?
x: Stabilisation corrects short-term imbalances (fiscal deficit, inflation, BoP) through demand management; structural adjustment is the supply side.

s: Which plan began immediately after the phase of structural adjustment and macroeconomic stabilisation?
x: The Eighth Plan, covering 1992–97, began after structural adjustment and macroeconomic stabilisation.

s: Which one of the following pairs correctly identifies the lead institutions associated with stabilisation and structural adjustment respectively?
x: Stabilisation is linked with the IMF, whereas structural adjustment is linked with the World Bank, particularly the IBRD.

s: Which of the following sets contains only structural adjustment measures?
o: Delicensing, tariff reduction and public-sector disinvestment
Subsidy cuts, tight money and devaluation
Inflation control, deficit reduction and tight money
Demand management, exchange control and subsidy expansion
x: Delicensing, tariff reduction and public-sector disinvestment are structural measures aimed at improving supply-side efficiency and long-term growth.

s: Which of the following was a usual condition of IMF-World Bank Structural Adjustment Programmes?
x: SAP conditions included austerity, privatisation, deregulation, currency devaluation and better tax collection.

s: What is the nature of structural adjustment under the 1991 reforms?
x: Structural adjustment is long-term and supply-side, while stabilisation is short-term and demand-side.

s: What did delicensed firms get after the 1991 delicensing?
o: Freedom in pricing but curbs on expansion
Price controls and curbs on expansion
Price controls but no curbs on expansion
Freedom in pricing and no curbs on expansion
x: Delicensed firms gained pricing freedom and faced no expansion curbs; licensing stayed only for a few (5-6) industries.

s: What happened to the MRTP asset limits under the Industrial Policy of 1991?
x: The 1991 policy abolished MRTP asset limits, pre-entry restrictions and merger/expansion controls.

s: For what purpose was the Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) set up?
x: BIFR was established for the revival and rehabilitation of sick industrial units.

s: When was the National Renewal Fund set up?
x: The National Renewal Fund was set up in February 1992 as a safety net for workers.

s: What was the main objective of the National Renewal Fund?
o: Retraining and redeployment of workers hit by restructuring
x: The NRF aimed at retraining, redeploying and compensating workers affected by modernisation; BIFR handled sick units.

s: In practice, for what was the National Renewal Fund mostly used?
o: Voluntary Retirement Schemes in central PSUs
x: The NRF was mostly spent on VRS in central PSUs and was later limited to public sector units.

s: To how many did the 1991 Industrial Policy cut the industries reserved for the public sector from 17?
x: Public-sector reserved industries fell from 17 (1956 policy) to 8, later pruned further.

s: When was the New Industrial Policy announced?
x: The New Industrial Policy was announced on 24 July 1991.

s: Up to what limit did the 1991 Industrial Policy allow automatic approval of FDI in high-priority industries?
x: FDI up to 51% got automatic approval in high-priority industries in 1991; it is now 100% in most sectors.

s: After the 1991 Industrial Policy and later changes, about how many industries now need a compulsory licence?
x: Licensing now covers only 5-6 hazardous and strategic industries.

s: Which of the following was NOT a fiscal policy measure of 1991?
x: The tax net was widened, not contracted; expenditure control, subsidy cuts and better tax collection were part of the package.

s: Which of the following was a fiscal policy measure of 1991?
x: 1991 fiscal measures included expenditure control, subsidy cuts and better tax collection; the tax net was widened, not contracted.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 1991 fiscal policy measures:
1. Public expenditure was controlled.
2. The tax net was contracted.
3. Peak income and corporate tax rates were lowered.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Expenditure control and lower peak tax rates (Chelliah) were part of 1991; the tax net was widened, so 2 is wrong.

s: What does the criticism of 'jobless growth' against India's post-1991 growth mean?
o: Unemployment was eliminated but output stagnated
x: Jobless growth means output grew much faster than jobs, so many people, including graduates, ended up in gig work. Employment rising faster than output is the reverse. A fall in both is a recession, and stagnant output with no unemployment does not describe the criticism.

s: A persistent current account deficit has been identified as a structural cause of which of the following in India?
x: Persistent CAD has been identified as a structural cause of India's high cost of capital.

s: Which adverse outcome was associated with the pattern of growth after economic reforms?
o: Growth became entirely dependent on public-sector employment.
Agriculture received all investment and labour-intensive sectors disappeared.
Capital-intensive sectors generated more jobs than the available labour force.
Agriculture was neglected and capital-intensive growth generated too few jobs.
x: The pattern of growth was criticised for neglecting agriculture and concentrating growth in capital-intensive sectors, which created too few employment opportunities.

s: Which of the following best illustrates the criticism of crony capitalism?
o: Agricultural investment increases uniformly across regions
Small firms exclusively control public-sector disinvestment
All firms receive equal access to public resources
Gains are concentrated among large, politically connected firms
x: Crony capitalism is criticised because economic gains become concentrated among large firms with political connections.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's growth after 1991:
1. Poverty ratios declined.
2. Income and regional inequality narrowed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Post-1991 growth cut poverty ratios but widened income and regional inequality.

s: In which year did India's current account deficit peak at 4.8% of GDP?
x: The CAD peaked at 4.8% of GDP in FY13; it was 0.8% in H1 FY26.

s: What was the size of the Economic Stabilisation Fund announced after the $100 per barrel oil shock of March 2026?
x: A ₹57,381 crore Economic Stabilisation Fund was set up after the oil shock (14 March 2026).

s: Labour is placed in which List of the Constitution of India?
x: Labour is included in the Concurrent List, allowing both the Union and the States to legislate on the subject.

s: In which year did the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Central (Amendment) Rules extend fixed-term employment to all sectors?
x: The 2018 Amendment Rules extended fixed-term employment to all sectors and removed the termination notice for temporary workmen.

s: Which of the following is the correct number of Central laws merged into the four Labour Codes?
x: The four Labour Codes merged 29 Central labour laws.

s: The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 is subsumed in which Labour Code?
x: The Code on Wages includes the Equal Remuneration Act; the IR Code has the Trade Unions Act, the SS Code the Employees' Compensation Act, the OSH Code the Factories Act.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: OSH and Working Conditions Code — 13 laws
x: The Industrial Relations Code subsumed three laws, not four. The Code on Social Security, OSH Code and Code on Wages subsumed 9, 13 and 4 laws respectively.

s: Which Labour Code provides 26 weeks of maternity leave?
x: The Code on Social Security provides for 26 weeks of maternity leave.

s: Who fixes the national floor wage under the Code on Wages, 2019?
x: The Centre fixes the national floor wage; the Code also provides a universal minimum wage and bars gender discrimination.

s:
Consider the following statements about the threshold for prior permission for lay-off, retrenchment and closure:
1. It was raised from 100 to 300 workers.
2. The change was made by the Code on Wages, 2019.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 (not the Code on Wages) raised the threshold from 100 to 300 workers.

s:
Consider the following statements about the four Labour Codes:
1. They were operationalised from 21 November 2025.
2. Draft central rules for the Codes were released in December 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Codes came into force on 21 November 2025; draft central rules came in December 2025, not 2024.

s: Which is the only one of the four Labour Codes enacted in 2019?
x: Only the Code on Wages is of 2019; the other three Codes are of 2020.

s: The Contract Labour Act, 1970 is subsumed in which Labour Code?
o: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
x: The Contract Labour Act went into the OSH Code, not the Code on Wages.

s: In which Labour Code is the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 subsumed?
x: The IR Code merged the Trade Unions, Standing Orders and Industrial Disputes Acts.

s: Under which Labour Code are gig and platform workers covered?
x: The Social Security Code covers gig and platform workers and 26-week maternity.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 2018 Standing Orders Rules:
1. They allowed fixed-term employment in all sectors.
2. They require a termination notice for temporary workmen.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The 2018 rules extended fixed-term employment to all sectors and need no termination notice for temporary workmen.

s: Which of the following pairs of Labour Code and number of laws merged is correctly matched?
x: The Codes merged 4 (Wages), 3 (IR), 9 (Social Security) and 13 (OSH) laws.

s: Which committee recommended a national minimum wage of ₹375 per day?
x: The Anoop Satpathy Committee (2019) recommended a national minimum wage of ₹375 a day.

s: In which Labour Code is the Trade Unions Act, 1926 subsumed?
x: The Industrial Relations Code merged the Trade Unions Act, the Standing Orders Act and the Industrial Disputes Act.

s: Who is the 'occupier' of a factory under the Factories Act, 1948?
o: The person who has ultimate control over the factory
The factory manager appointed by the State
The largest shareholder of the company
x: Under Section 2(n), the occupier is the person with ultimate control; in a company a director must be named.

s: In which Labour Code are the EPF and ESI laws subsumed?
x: The Social Security Code merges 9 laws, including EPF, ESI and Employees' Compensation.

s: In which Labour Code is the Factories Act, 1948 subsumed?
o: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
x: The OSH Code merges 13 laws, including the Factories Act and the Contract Labour Act.

s: In which year was the Industrial Disputes Act enacted?
x: The Industrial Disputes Act is of 1947; it is now in the Industrial Relations Code, 2020.

s: The pillars of the next-generation reforms begin with which two factor markets?
x: The stated pillars begin with land, including easier acquisition, and labour, including simpler laws.

s: Which of the following pairs of reform measure and generation is correctly matched?
o: Tariff cuts and removal of import licensing – Second generation
Fully functional Panchayati Raj Institutions – First generation
x: Factor-market reforms are second-generation; tariff cuts and delicensing are first-generation; functional PRIs are third-generation reforms.

s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of initiatives for digitising land records?
x: DILRMP, ULPIN and NGDRS are associated with digitising land records.

s: In the factor-market reform framework, under which head are the IBC and capital-market reform classed?
x: The framework covers land (land-record digitisation), labour (four Labour Codes) and capital (IBC and capital-market reform).

s: Which of the following is NOT an area of second-generation reforms?
o: Factor markets such as land, labour and capital
x: Tariff cuts and delicensing were first-generation reforms of 1991-2000; the others are second-generation areas.

s: Which Article provides restrictions relating to taxation of supplies outside a State and import-export?
x: Article 286 limits States from taxing supplies outside the State or in the course of import and export. Article 269A covers IGST on inter-State supply.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the GST Council?
x: Article 279A provides for the GST Council; 246A gives the power to levy GST, 269A covers IGST and 366(12A) defines GST.

s: When did the Goods and Services Tax come into force in India?
x: GST came into force on 1 July 2017.

s: Which of the following taxes subsumed under GST was a State tax rather than a Central tax?
x: Central excise, service tax and CST were Central taxes subsumed under GST; State VAT was a State tax.

s: Which was the first State to ratify the Constitution Amendment relating to GST?
x: Assam was the first State to ratify the GST amendment; GST follows the Canadian dual model and traces to the Vijay Kelkar Committee.

s: What special slab for sin and luxury goods did Next-Generation GST (GST 2.0), announced in August 2025, introduce?
x: GST 2.0 brought rate rationalisation and a 40% slab for sin and luxury goods; input tax credit was retained.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for IGST on inter-State supply?
x: Article 269A covers IGST; 246A gives the power to levy GST and 279A creates the GST Council.

s: India's GST follows which model of dual GST?
x: India adopted the Canadian dual model, recommended by the Kelkar Committee.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about GST?
o: It subsumed State VAT and service tax
x: GST is destination-based, not origin-based; the other statements are correct.

s: Which Constitution Amendment Act inserted Article 246A, the constitutional basis for GST laws by Parliament and the States?
x: The 101st Constitution Amendment Act, 2016 inserted Article 246A.

s: Which committee is linked with the idea of GST in India?
x: The Kelkar Committee (task force) proposed GST; it came through the 101st Amendment.

s: The Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016 on GST was introduced as which Bill?
x: The 101st Amendment Act was the 122nd Amendment Bill.

s: Which committee (1993) recommended private entry into India's insurance sector?
x: The Malhotra Committee (1993) recommended private entry, leading to the IRDA Act 1999.

s: In which year was the IRDA Act, which followed the Malhotra Committee's recommendations, passed?
x: The Malhotra Committee (1993) led to the IRDA Act of 1999.

s: To what limit did the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha Act, 2025 raise FDI in insurance?
x: The 2025 Act raised insurance FDI from 74% to 100%.

s: India's better Market Distortions Performance Index position was credited to GST, trade facilitation and which other reform?
x: GST, the IBC and trade facilitation were credited; import quotas and similar restrictions were not.

s: NITI Aayog was set up in 2015 to replace the Planning Commission and to promote which of the following?
x: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission and promotes cooperative and competitive federalism.

s: What tax rate did the September 2019 corporate tax cut give to new manufacturing units?
x: The 2019 cut set 22 per cent for existing companies and 15 per cent for new manufacturing units.

s: What is the main purpose of the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023?
o: Ranking of States on business reforms
x: The Jan Vishwas Act, 2023 decriminalised minor offences to ease compliance.

s: India's rank in the World Bank's Doing Business ranking improved from 142 in 2014 to what?
x: India's World Bank Doing Business rank improved from 142 in 2014 to 63 in 2019.

s: Andhra Pradesh has ranked first since which edition of the Business Reforms Action Plan?
x: Andhra Pradesh has ranked number one since BRAP 2016.

s: To which of the following is the Single Desk Portal in Andhra Pradesh linked?
o: Andhra Pradesh Power Distribution Recapitalisation Fund
x: The Single Desk Portal is linked to the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor ease-of-doing-business loan.

s: What does the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, spread over 14 sectors, mainly aim to boost?
x: PLI (₹1.97 lakh crore, 14 sectors) targets manufacturing and exports.

s: When were the three Farm Acts of September 2020 repealed?
x: The Farm Acts of September 2020 were repealed in November 2021.

s: Strategic disinvestment is the main objective of which of the following?
x: The New Public Sector Enterprise Policy 2021 is about strategic disinvestment.

s: When was Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), later linked to the JAM trinity, launched?
x: DBT began on 1 January 2013 and was later built on JAM.

s: Under UDAY (2015), States took over what share of DISCOM debt?
x: Under UDAY, States absorbed 75% of DISCOM debt.

s: Which of the following pairs of reform and its feature is correctly matched?
o: UDAY – Smart meters and ACS-ARR gap zero
EASE – Reform agenda for public sector banks
x: EASE (Jan 2018) is the PSB reform agenda; Indradhanush was ₹70,000 crore, UDAY is the debt takeover and RDSS covers smart meters and the ACS-ARR gap.

s: What AT&C loss level does the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS, 2021-26) target?
x: RDSS aims to cut AT&C losses to 12-15% and close the ACS-ARR gap.

s: Under which plan were public sector banks given ₹70,000 crore of capital in August 2015?
x: Indradhanush (August 2015) provided ₹70,000 crore to recapitalise PSBs.

s: What is the outlay of the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (2021-26)?
x: RDSS has an outlay of ₹3,03,758 crore to cut AT&C losses to 12-15%.

s: How large was the public sector bank recapitalisation plan announced in October 2017?
x: The October 2017 plan was ₹2.11 lakh crore, of which ₹1.35 lakh crore came via recap bonds.

s: Under the National Monetisation Pipeline, which assets are monetised and how?
o: Greenfield assets sold permanently to private parties
Brownfield assets sold permanently through strategic sale
Brownfield, de-risked assets leased via OMT and InvITs, with ownership retained by government
Greenfield assets leased with ownership transferred to operators
x: NMP leases brownfield, de-risked assets through OMT and InvITs; ownership stays with the government and assets return after the lease.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the approximate NMP sectoral shares?
x: The approximate shares are roads 27 per cent, railways 25 per cent and power 15 per cent.

s: When was the National Monetisation Pipeline (₹6 lakh crore over FY2022-25) formally launched?
x: The NMP was announced in the Budget 2021-22 (February 2021) and launched in August 2021; it covers brownfield core assets of central ministries and CPSEs.

s: Within how many days must the corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) under the IBC 2016 normally be completed?
x: CIRP has 180 days, with one 90-day extension allowed.

s: After the 2019 amendment, what is the outer limit for completing the CIRP under the IBC?
x: The 2019 amendment set an outer limit of 330 days (180 + 90 plus litigation time).

s:
Consider the following statements about institutions under the IBC 2016:
1. The NCLT adjudicates insolvency cases.
2. The IBBI regulates the insolvency process.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The NCLT is the adjudicating authority and the IBBI is the regulator; both statements are correct.

s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016?
o: Maximisation of the value of assets
Promotion of entrepreneurship and availability of credit
x: The Code seeks time-bound resolution, maximising asset value, and promoting entrepreneurship and credit; nationalisation is not an aim.

s: Which of the following was the largest export item of India in 2024-25 by share?
x: Petroleum products constituted the largest listed export item in 2024-25, with a share of 14.48 percent.

s: Which group has been India's largest agricultural export in recent years?
x: Marine products led agri exports in 1997-98 to 1999-2000, but cereals (chiefly rice) are the largest in recent years.

s: About what share of the world's polished diamonds does India export?
x: India exports about 75% of the world's polished diamonds, thanks to its skill in cutting and polishing.

s: What was the value of India's electronics exports in 2024-25?
x: Electronics exports grew 32.46% to $38.56 bn in 2024-25.

s: Which product made up about 62.5% of India's electronics exports in 2024-25?
x: Smartphones were 62.5% of India's electronics exports in 2024-25.

s: Which of the following statements reflects recent changes in the direction of India's trade?
o: Crude imports were concentrated in a single source.
Labour-intensive exports and crude-import sources remained unchanged.
Labour-intensive exports shifted towards only the United States.
Labour-intensive exports shifted from the US towards the Middle East, Africa, Europe and Asia, and crude sources diversified.
x: Labour-intensive exports moved from the US towards the Middle East, Africa, Europe and Asia, while crude-import sources were diversified.

s: On the basis of the 2024-25 direction-of-trade data, India ran a trade surplus with which of the following groups?
x: India ran a surplus with the United States and the Netherlands. It ran deficits with China, Russia, the UAE and Saudi Arabia because imports exceeded exports with those partners.

s: Which of the following is NOT listed as a response to India's dependence on China for APIs, solar cells and chips?
x: The listed responses are QCOs, NTBs and PLI. Abolition of all import regulations is not listed as a response.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's trade with China?
o: China supplies about 16% of India's imports.
India imports iron ore from China as a major item.
China supplies APIs and solar cells to India.
India exports iron ore, cotton and marine products to China.
x: India does not import iron ore; it exports iron ore, including to China.

s: Which country was India's largest overall trading partner in FY 2025-26?
x: China became India's largest overall trading partner, while the United States remained its largest export market.

s: With which country did India have its largest trade surplus ($35.32 bn) in 2024-25?
x: India's largest trade surplus is with the USA; it runs deficits with UAE and Saudi Arabia.

s: Which of the following was India's largest source of imports in 2024-25?
x: China was India’s largest import source in 2024-25, accounting for 15.73 percent of imports.

s: In which year was the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) formed?
x: The GCC was formed in 1981 by Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.

s: In 2018, which of the following, taken as a bloc, received the largest share of India's exports?
x: The EU as a bloc took the most Indian exports in 2018; the USA was the top single country.

s: Which country was India's largest export market among BRICS members in FY 2025-26?
x: UAE was India's largest BRICS export market ($37.4 bn) in FY26.

s: Which of the following groups accounted for approximately one-third of India’s imports in 2024-25?
o: Crude petroleum, gold and petroleum products
x: Crude petroleum, gold and petroleum products together accounted for approximately one-third of India’s imports.

s: Which of the following is classified as a non-bulk import?
x: Capital goods are included among non-bulk imports. Crude and petroleum products, cereals, pulses, edible oils, sugar, fertiliser, metals and ores are listed as bulk imports.

s: Which of the following statements about India's import basket is incorrect?
o: Crude oil and petroleum products (POL) are India's largest import item by value.
Gold is among India's major import items.
Electronic goods are among India's major import items.
Pulses are India's largest import item by value.
x: Option D is incorrect: pulses are a small import; crude oil and petroleum products are India's largest import by value, followed by items such as electronic goods and gold.

s: How are export promotion and import substitution respectively described?
x: Import substitution is an inward-looking strategy, whereas export promotion is an outward-looking strategy.
